questions.question: Three axes are turning each other using straps. Which axis will turn faster?
questions.explanation: 1. Note the setup: three wheels, each on its own axis, linked by two belts. 2. Recall the rule: when wheels of different sizes are connected, the larger wheel turns more slowly, because it covers more distance per turn while a smaller wheel must turn more often to cover the same distance. 3. Compare the wheels: wheel 2 is smaller than wheels 1 and 3. 4. Conclude: the smallest wheel turns fastest, so wheel 2 is the fastest. The correct answer is 2.

scene.note: Three belt pulleys side by side, all turning clockwise (curved arrows on top). Wheel 1 on the left is largest, wheel 2 in the middle is smallest, wheel 3 on the right is medium. An open belt connects wheel 1 to wheel 2, and a second open belt connects wheel 2 to wheel 3, so all turn the same way; the smallest pulley (2) spins fastest.

questions.question: In which figure does one need to exert more force to lift the weight ? If the force exerted is equal please select answer option 3.
questions.explanation: 1. Recall what a pulley is: a wheel on an axle with a rope running over it. 2. Recall the fixed pulley rule: it gives no force advantage; it only changes the direction of the force. 3. Recall the movable pulley rule: it lets you use less force, because the rope pulls it upward on both sides at once, so the weight is shared equally and the pulley puts half the load on the ceiling. 4. Extend the idea: with three supporting rope sections, only one third of the force is needed, and so on. 5. Compare the options: option 1 has a single fixed pulley, while option 2 adds a movable pulley, and both pull in the same direction. 6. Conclude: option 1 has no force advantage, so it needs more force. The correct answer is 1.

scene.note: Two ceiling pulley rigs lifting identical weights. Figure 1 (left): one fixed pulley on the ceiling, rope from the weight up over it, free end pulled down — no mechanical advantage. Figure 2 (right): one fixed ceiling pulley plus one movable pulley attached above the weight, rope sharing the load on both sides of the movable pulley — half the force needed.

questions.question: On which pole does the weight press harder? If equal, choose 3.
questions.explanation: 1. Identify the pivot: the rectangle turns about its point of contact with the floor. 2. Recall the lever principle: the farther a pole is from the pivot, the less force it needs to produce the same torque. 3. Compare the poles: pole 2 is farther from the point of contact than pole 1, so pole 2 applies less force. 4. Apply Newton's third law: the rectangle pushes back on pole 2 with equally less force. 5. Conclude: the weight presses harder on pole 1. The correct answer is 1.

scene.note: Two identical tilted rectangular blocks, each resting with its lower right corner on the floor (the pivot) and propped from below by a short vertical pole. In figure 1 the pole is close to the floor contact point; in figure 2 the pole is farther left, farther from the pivot. The block presses harder on the nearer pole (1).

questions.question: What changes to the electrical circuit would increase the current measurement at point D?
questions.explanation: The current is in a series circuit, both total current and current through individual resistors, is directly dependent upon the battery voltage and inversely dependent upon the total circuit resistance. The current can be increased by increasing the battery voltage or by decreasing the total resistance. The correct answer is Reduce one bulb's resistance.

questions.question: Which shelf can carry more weight? (If equal, choose 3.)
questions.explanation: 1. Break the cable's force into two parts: a vertical part and a horizontal part. 2. Recognize which part matters: only the vertical part actually holds the load up. 3. See the effect of the angle: the smaller the angle between the cable and the shelf, the larger the horizontal part and the smaller the vertical part, so the cable must pull harder overall. 4. Picture the extremes: a fully vertical cable is the most efficient, while a fully horizontal cable can't hold the shelf at all. 5. Conclude: the shelf with the larger cable angle carries more weight. The correct answer is 2.

questions.explanation: 1. Car one is on the outer side of the bend, which is a longer path than car two's inner side. 2. To stay level with car two, car one must cover that greater distance in the same time. 3. So car one must travel faster. The correct answer is option one.

questions.explanation: 1. Compare the blades: ventilator 2 has more blades than ventilator 1. 2. Note the effect: more blades meet more air resistance. 3. Conclude: ventilator 2 needs a stronger engine to spin its blades at the same speed. The answer is 2.

questions.question: Which wheel will turn faster? If both wheels turn at the same speed please select answer option '3'.
questions.explanation: 1. Recall the rule: when wheels of different sizes are connected, the larger wheel turns more slowly, because a smaller wheel must turn more often to cover the same distance. 2. Compare the wheels: wheel 1 is smaller than wheel 2. 3. Conclude: the smaller wheel turns faster, so wheel 1 is faster. The correct answer is 1.

scene.note: A flat board/plank rests on top of two rollers/wheels on the ground, shown in perspective. Wheel 1 on the left is small; wheel 2 on the right is much larger. Both are driven by the same board movement, so the smaller wheel 1 must rotate faster.

questions.question: The three cogwheels are joined and are moving very quickly. Which wheel is moving faster than the others?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (C) – 3. Wheel 3 is the smallest in diameter, so it will move faster than the others.

scene.note: Three meshed cogwheels in a row. Wheel 1 on the left is medium, wheel 2 in the middle is the largest, wheel 3 on the right is the smallest. All mesh directly, so the smallest wheel (3) rotates fastest.

questions.question: Complete the following: If 4 Coulombs of charge flow past point A in 2 seconds, then ___ Coulombs of charge flow through point B in 4 seconds.
questions.explanation: For a steady flow of charge through a surface, the current can be calculated with the formula: I=Q/t , with I indicating current, Q the electric charge transferred through the surface and t the duration of the transfer. I is measured in Amperes, Q in Coulombs and t in seconds. Therefore, if 4 coulombs pass through point A in 2 seconds, the current is: I = 4 Q / 2 s, or: I = 2 Q / s, which is 2 Amperes.

questions.question: Which figure depicts the right trajectory of the bomb being dropped?
questions.explanation: 1. When a bomb is dropped, two influences act on it at once: its forward motion and the constant downward pull of gravity. 2. The bomb's forward speed gradually decreases over time, while gravity stays constant, so gravity's relative influence grows. 3. Because of this, the bomb's path bends into a curved, ballistic trajectory rather than a straight line. 4. The correct answer is option two.

questions.explanation: 1. Compare the loads: cart 1's load sits higher than cart 2's. 2. Note the effect: a higher load means a higher center of gravity. 3. Conclude: a higher center of gravity makes cart 1 more likely to flip. The answer is 1.

questions.question: If the small weight balances the bigger weight and the two small weights in both figures are equal in weight, which of the bigger weights is heavier? If the bigger weights weigh the same please select answer option '3'.
questions.explanation: 1. Recall the balance rule: the heavier the big weight, the farther out the small weight must sit to balance it. 2. Look at Figure 2: its small weight sits fairly close to the axis yet still balances the big weight, so that big weight must be lighter. 3. Conclude: the heavier weight is in Figure 1. The answer is 1.

scene.note: Two balance beams on triangular fulcrums, each with a large hanging weight (blue block) on the left and a small weight on top of the right arm. Figure 1 (left): the small weight sits far out near the end of the right arm to balance. Figure 2 (right): the small weight sits close to the fulcrum yet still balances. Equal small weights, so Figure 1's big weight is heavier.

questions.question: Which rope can hold the weight on its own?
questions.explanation: The weight is pulling the axis down and lifting the opposite side up. For the rope to hold the weight it must exert the same amount of force the weight is exerting but in the opposite direction. The only rope that does this is rope 2. The answer is 2

scene.note: A vertical post with a horizontal beam crossing it near the top, pivoting on the post; a weight sits on the right end of the beam, pulling that side down and lifting the left side up. Three diagonal ropes are candidates: rope 1 runs from the top of the post down-left to the left end of the beam (upper left), rope 2 runs from lower on the post up-left to the left end of the beam (lower left), rope 3 runs from the post down-right under the beam. Only rope 2 pulls opposite to the weight's torque and can hold it alone.

questions.question: If the left cogwheel rotates in the direction of the arrow, in which direction does the right wheel rotate? Please select answer option '3' if the wheel doesn't turn.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (A) – 1. The cogwheels turn in opposite directions. When the left wheel turns in the direction of the arrow (counterclockwise), the middle wheel will turn to the right (clockwise). This will cause the right wheel to turn counterclockwise.

scene.note: Three equal meshed cogwheels in a row. The left wheel has a counterclockwise arrow. Two direction options are marked over the right wheel: 1 = counterclockwise (same sense as the left wheel), 2 = clockwise. Meshing reverses direction at each contact, so the right wheel turns counterclockwise, option 1.

questions.question: Which side of the road will the car slide towards when it takes the turn? If the car won't slide please select answer option '3'.
questions.explanation: 1. When a car takes a turn, the centrifugal force pushes it outward, away from the centre. 2. So the car slides toward the outer rim. The correct answer is option one.

questions.explanation: 1. Cogwheels that touch must turn in opposite directions. 2. So neither outer wheel can turn the same way as the middle wheel. 3. The answer is option three, neither of them.

questions.question: If the ball follows the arrow on the billiard table, which ball will it hit?
questions.explanation: 1. When a ball bounces off a cushion, the angle at which it arrives equals the angle at which it leaves. 2. Because of this equal-angle rule, the ball's path after bouncing off the far side runs parallel to its original approach line. 3. In this example, the geometry shows the two angles adding up to one hundred eighty degrees, which confirms the before and after lines are parallel. 4. The only target that lies along this parallel path is ball two, so the correct answer is option two. 5. Note that the picture may look slightly inaccurate, but these tests deliberately draw images loosely, so the answer must come from the physical principle rather than the exact drawing.

questions.explanation: 1. Recall that in circular motion the angular velocity is the same at every point on the wheel. 2. Recall that the linear velocity changes with distance from the center: points farther out cover more distance in the same time. 3. Compare the points: point 2 is farther from the center than point 1. 4. Conclude: point 2 has the greater linear velocity.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is 3. When switching the electrical switch on, the electrical circuit will be closed and bulb 3 will light up. From A to B to C to D

questions.question: Which fisherman has to pull his fishing rod with more force in order to lift the caught fish?
choices: Both have to apply equal forces
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (A) – 1. The difference between the two fishermen is the gripping point in which they hold the rod. Fisherman 1 holds the rod at the bottom end, and therefore, the total weight he must pull is greater: the fish and the entire length of the rod. Fisherman 2 holds the rod in the middle, and therefore, the total weight he must pull is smaller: the fish and only half of the rod's length. Moreover, the weight of the rod below the gripping point will assist in the pulling of the fish.

scene.note: Two fishermen each holding a fishing rod (lever) with a fish hanging from the tip. Fisherman 1 (left) grips the rod at its bottom end; fisherman 2 (right) grips his rod in the middle. Fish hangs from the far tip of each rod.

questions.question: A dynamometer is used for measuring force. What can be assumed about dynamometers A and B in the following figures?
choices: A will show a lower reading
B will show a lower reading
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (A) – A will show a lower reading. In this question, the lever is a class 2 lever in which the load is between the fulcrum and the effort. The fulcrum is the fixed pivot at the left side of the lever, the load is the mass weighing 10Kg and the effort is the force required to balance the weight of the mass which is measured by the dynamometer. Here, it is the position of the load that changes between the two figures. Since the work, or more precisely torque, is constant, the shorter the distance between the load and the fulcrum, the lighter the load, the smaller the force required to lift it, and the lower the reading of the dynamometer. Therefore, dynamometer A will show a lower reading is the correct answer.

scene.note: Two horizontal lever arms, each pivoted at the left end (fulcrum) and held up at the right end by a dynamometer. A: a 10kg mass hangs close to the fulcrum (near the middle-left of the arm). B: an identical 10kg mass hangs at the far right end of the arm, farther from the fulcrum.

questions.question: Complete the following: Should the resistance of the bell located between points A and B increase, the current going through the second bell will ___.

questions.question: Two weights are placed on the right side of a lever, as shown in the picture below. What mass would you place 20 cm to the left of the fulcrum, in order to balance the lever?
questions.explanation: For the scale to balance, the total of torques on either side of the scale must be equal. Assigning the numbers 1, 2, and 3 to the weights of 5kg, 6kg, and the "?" weight respectively, we have our torque equation: T₁ + T₂ = T₃. Each torque is by definition T = W x L, where W is the weight and L is the distance from the fulcrum. Recall that W = M x g, where M is the mass and g is the gravitational constant. M₁ x g x L₁ + M₂ x g x L₂ = M₃ x g x L₃ We can simplify by dividing both sides by g: M₁ x L₁ + M₂ x L₂ = M₃ x L₃ Our givens are M₁ = 5kg, L₁ = 12cm, M₂ = 6kg, L₂ = 15cm, M₃ = ?, L₃ = 20cm. Substituting the values given in the question in the equation: 5kg x 12cm + 6kg x 15cm = M₃ x 20cm [explanation continues past the bottom of the captured shot]

questions.explanation: The lever is also a class 1 in which the fulcrum is between the load and the effort. It is given in the question that the distance between the two masses is 15 cm. In order to solve the question the distance between the mass weighing 4 kg and the fulcrum will be marked as the variable d and the distance between the mass weighing 8 kg and the fulcrum as 15 cm - d. The answer is calculated by substituting the values given in the question in the below equation: M₁ × L₁ = M₂ × L₂ 4 kg × d = 8 kg × (15 cm - d) 4d = 120 - 8d Therefore: d = 10 cm Therefore, 10 cm is the correct answer.

questions.question: Approximately how much force is required to lift the mass weighting 800 N?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 50N. Let's first observe a simpler system. Instead of 4 movable pulleys, we try solving for only 1. Any force we apply will be carried across the rope. The rope wraps around the pulley, pulling it upward twice (once from each side). Therefore, any force we apply will be applied twofold to the weight. If this was the system in question, the answer would have been 800N / 2 = 400N. Now we extend this logic. If we put another movable pulley before the weight, the force we apply will double once more before reaching the load. Each pulley we add doubles the force we apply. Thus, 4 pulleys will double the force we apply 4 times, so we need only apply a force 2*2*2*2=16 times less than the load. 800N / 16 = 50N, which is the answer. Note that the rightmost pulley is not taken into account because it is a fixed pulley, and does not divide force, only changes its direction.

questions.question: How far does the mass rise when the rope is pulled for 6 cm? (All pulleys are fixed except for the pulley supporting the mass directly)
questions.explanation: 1. Recall the rule: lifting force equals the load divided by the number of rope sections supporting it. 2. Count the supporting sections: the load is supported by two, so the force is halved. The rope sections on the last two pulleys don't support the load. 3. Recall the trade-off: less force means the rope must be pulled farther than the load moves, in exact inverse proportion. 4. Apply it: the rope is pulled 6 centimeters, so the mass rises 6 divided by 2. 5. Conclude: the mass rises 3 centimeters. The correct answer is 3 centimeters.

One rope runs through all of them; the free end leaves the top-right pulley diagonally downward (pull direction arrow). Only the pulley supporting the mass is movable; the mass is held by 2 rope sections.

questions.question: Approximately how much force is required to hold a mass weighing 360 N?
questions.explanation: In this case, all three movable pulleys are connected to the mass, and the same rope is wrapped around all three, so the rope pulls the mass six times. Since the tension is equal along the entire rope, the weight is divided equally between the six parts of the rope. (Again, if you do not feel comfortable with this explanation try to draw a simple force diagram) In this question the load is a mass weighting 360N, therefore, a force of 360 N/ 6 = 60 N is required to lift the load and 60 N is the correct answer.

questions.question: A force of 10 N(Newton) compresses two identical springs in parallel for 8 cm. What will be the total distance that four identical springs in series are compressed?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (D) - 64 cm An external force exerted on a spring causes it to compress or extend. The distance of compression or extension is directly and linearly proportional to the force exerted on the spring, i.e., doubling the force causes the spring to stretch or compress twice as much. When identical springs are connected in parallel, the applied force is divided equally between them. Consider the image below: Each of the two springs connected in parallel is subjected to a force of 5 N that compresses each spring by 8 cm (1). On the other hand, had only one spring been subjected to a 10N force, it would compress by 16 cm (2). When identical springs are connected in series, the entire force is applied to each spring separately. Consider the image below: Each of the four springs in series is subjected to a force of 10 N, and therefore resembles the case in image (2), compressing 16 cm. questions.question: This shape is stamped out of a continuous stainless steel coil with a width of 55 cm in order to create components for airplanes. The stamping process requires a gap of 20 mm between each two adjacent components. The coil is supplied in lengths of 40 meters costing 400$ each. Assuming minimal wastage, how many components can be produced from each 40 m coil?
questions.explanation: According to the sketch given above the length of the component is 50 cm and its width is: 20 cm + 40 cm = 60 cm. As mentioned above the width of the stainless steel coil is 55 cm and its length is 4000 cm (remember that 1 m equals 100 cm). The width of a single component is longer than that of the coil and therefore each component is stamped out of the coil in an angle of 90⁰ clockwise compared to the sketch of the component given above. Thus, the width and length of the component are switched so that the width of a single component is now 50 and its length is 60 cm. Taking into account the gap of 20 mm between each two adjacent component the length of a single unit for stamping is: 60 cm + 2 cm = 62 cm (remember that 1 cm equals 10 mm). Thus, If the length of the coil is 4000 cm and the length of a single unit is 62 cm, under the assumption of minimal wastage the number of components produced is: 4000 cm /62 cm = 64.5 ~ 64 components. Therefore, 64 is the correct answer.

questions.question: These components are stamped out of a continuous stainless steel coil with a width of 55 cm. The stamping process requires a gap of 20 mm between each two adjacent components. The coil is supplied in lengths of 40 meters costing 400$ each. What is the approximate percentage of stainless steel wasted?
questions.explanation: The area of the stainless steel coil is: 55 cm × 4000 cm = 220000 cm². According to the first in this question set, the area of each component is 1828 cm² and according to the second question, the number of components stamped out of the coil is 64. Thus, the area of all components is: 64 × 1828 cm² = 116992 cm². The percentage of stainless steel used for producing the components is: 116992 cm² / 220000 cm² × 100 ~ 53%. Therefore, the percentage of stainless steel wasted is 100% - 53% = 47% and 47% is the correct answer.

questions.question: What is the approximate cost of a component if the scrap is sold at 50% of cost?
questions.explanation: As mentioned previously, the cost of a single stainless steel coil is 400$. Thus, the value of the scrap is 400$ × 50/100 = 200$ per coil. We shall calculate the percentage of stainless steel wasted: Waste(%) = 100 - Used(%) Used(%) = ((Components made) X (Component Area) / (Coil Area)) X 100 = ((64 X 1828) / (4000 X 55)) X 100 = (116,992 / 220,000) X 100 = 53% Waste(%) = 100 - 53 = 47% The waste percentage is 47%. Thus, the cost of all the components is: 400$ - (47/100 × 200$) = 306$. Therefore, the cost of a single component is: 306$/64 ~ 4.8$ and 4.8$ is the correct answer.

questions.question: How does wheel B rotate if wheel A rotates clockwise at a constant velocity?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (B) – Clockwise, greater velocity. When gears such as wheels are connected by a belt or a rolling chain they rotate in the same direction. However, if the belt or chain is crossed the gears rotate in opposite directions. In this question, the initial three wheels are connected by a single belt. Since wheel A rotates clockwise, all three wheels rotate clockwise. The upper right wheel is connected to the fourth wheel by a crossed belt and thus, it rotates anti-clockwise. The fifth greater wheel is connected to the fourth wheel by a straight belt and hence they both rotate anti-clockwise. Finally, the sixth smaller wheel B is connected to the fifth wheel by a crossed belt and therefore it rotates clockwise as the first greater wheel. This eliminates answers A and C. When two wheels (or gears) of equal diameters are combined they rotate at the same velocity. When two wheels of unequal diameters are combined the wheel with the greater diameter rotates slower. The ratio of their diameters (or equivalently, the ratio of their radii) is directly proportional to the gear ratio and is inversely proportional to the ratio of wheel velocities. In this question wheel B has a smaller diameter than wheel A. Therefore, Clockwise at a greater velocity is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which switches must be closed so that exactly three bulbs would light up?
questions.explanation: The answer is C. Leaving switch 1 open will prevent any current from flowing, thus no bulbs will light up. Therefore they will not light up, only the middle one, so option A is incorrect. Closing switch 2 will allow the current to flow through the left bulb, and closing switch 3 will allow current through the right bulb. Therefore, closing switch 1 and 2, or closing switch 1 and 3, will allow current through exactly 3 bulbs, as required, marking option C correct. Closing all switches will allow current through all 4 bulbs, marking option D incorrect.

questions.question: In which way is it easier to carry the large hammer? If it makes no difference then please select answer option 3.
questions.explanation: In this question the hammer functions as a lever in which the fulcrum is between the load and the effort. The fulcrum is the figure's shoulder balancing the hammer; the load is the mass of the hammer's head; and the effort is the force applied by the figure's hand that is required to balance the weight. We can see that the position of the fulcrum changes between the two figures. Since the weight of the load is constant, the shorter the distance between the load and the fulcrum the smaller the torque and subsequently so is the force required to balance it. The correct answer is 2.

scene.note: Two figures each carry a large hammer on the shoulder, which acts as the fulcrum of a lever; the hand applies the effort and the hammer head is the load. In figure 1 the hammer head is far from the shoulder (long load arm). In figure 2 the hammer head rests close to the shoulder (short load arm), so less force is needed — figure 2 is easier.

questions.question: On which of the chains is more tension being exerted? If the tensions are identical, choose option 3.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is (A) – 1. The tension of the chain must oppose and cancel out the force of gravity. That is, the vertical component of the tension exerted must be equal to the gravitational force. In option 1, the vertical component is only a part of the tension exerted by the chain (as it runs in an angle relative to the vertical direction). In option 2, the vertical component is the whole tension exerted by the chain (as it runs vertically). Therefore, the chain in Option 1 must exert more force than the chain in Option 2 in order to exert the same vertical force.

questions.question: Which pulley setup would reduce the amount of force required to lift the load? If there is no difference then select option 3.
